questions.problem:
Given that
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -5 & -1\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU$, then ${l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{12}=$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices: 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ \frac{5}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ \frac{5}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{5}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=-\frac{5}{2},{u}_{12}=1,$ and ${l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{12}=-\frac{5}{2}.$

$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU$, then ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=-1,{u}_{22}=0,$ and ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=-1.$

questions.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU$, then ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to reduce the matrix to the row echelon form. For every elementary row operation we also write the equivalent notation in terms of multiplication by the corresponding elementary matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=-2,{u}_{22}=0,$ and ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=-2.$
